replies.author: BlueAndYellowTowels
replies.body:
I don't see how it's a way to "benchmark the models". We have no idea of the actual time and effort. We have no idea of the process. We have no idea of the controls or context.

Benchmarking has actual measurements. Right? I know LLMs have benchmarks... they look nothing like this.

If an LLM can write code, even of moderate quality, you can create a game. No problem. The better model the better it gets as assuming the "gaps" the user forgets to tweak or define.

But, these so called "benchmarks" are no different than "which language is best" or "what engine should I use"... they're just... tools doing things.

This is not a game. The ability to create code, is not the same as the ability to create a game.

comments.author: Commercial-Drama-867
comments.body:
With the rate at which this stuff is progressing, it might not be too long because you can actually make a game like GTA 6 in a single prompt. 

If you look at the games these models could code a year ago, and look at what it can code now... it's a pretty massive leap... and if this trajectory continues... you'll be able to make your own AAA games by prompting in the not too distant future. It might take a few days and a lot of tokens... but with multiple agents working on various components of the game... it's not crazy to think you could get a AAA game within a day if you pay for the tokens.
